cloze.title: 原文选词填空
cloze.instruction: 从词库中选择合适的词填入空白，每词使用一次，保留原文词形。大小写不影响判分。

parts.text: For example, in a study involving a large online travel agency in China, more than 1,500 engineers, marketing and

staff were allowed to work from home on Wednesdays and Fridays, while a control group stayed in the office full time.

Over the following two years of performance reviews, the performance of the hybrid workers was

in quality to those who stayed in the office. And the ones who worked from home were much less likely to leave the company – especially women and the workers with long commutes.

A smaller

at an international development organisation went a step further, by randomly varying how many days 148 staff spent in the office.

Those who came in around two days a week said they had a better work-life balance, more job

and less isolation than colleagues who came in more or less often. Their performance was unaffected.

These studies (among others) suggest that a week split roughly half and half between home and office costs

little, while keeping staff happier and more likely to stay.

But there is also evidence that the office time counts, and that some work really does suffer at a

.

In experiments across five countries, researchers found that video calls can reduce the flow of creative ideas. And an analysis of 20 million research papers and 4 million patents found that remote teams were less likely to produce

. The evidence shows that being in the same room matters most when people are coming up with ideas together.

But that doesn’t mean office workers should be together all day every day. In the Chinese travel agency trial, staff in the office three days a week did just as well as those in for five. The

two days bought nothing measurable in performance – but more resignations.

Yet there is a risk that return-to-office rules set a minimum

of days with no maximum, so that the minimum number creeps up. A study of over 1,000 UK managers, found that employees working from home were less likely to be considered for promotion and pay rises. When being seen is
“at least three days” can quietly become four or five days for those who want to climb the career ladder.

reading.title: 主旨、理解与信息定位
reading.instruction: 阅读原文后回答 5 道选择题：1 道主旨、1 道内容理解、1 道段落细节、2 道信息定位。段落细节题以题干指定段落为准。

questions.prompt: Which statement best summarises the overall focus of this article?
options: Resilience beyond short household emergencies depends on stronger food supply chains.
Shopping early can provide practical benefits for both consumers and retailers.
Research on office attendance offers a more nuanced view of how often people should work on site.
Fireworks create environmental and economic costs that outlast the celebrations.
questions.explanation: 把标题与全文各段的中心内容连起来判断主旨，避免把同一主题下的其他话题当成本文重点。
questions.evidence: Office attendance from Monday to Friday used to be a pretty standard requirement for many jobs.

questions.prompt: What change did Barclays announce for the UK staff described?
options: A rule requiring seven office days every week
A reduction from five to zero days of any work
An increase from two to at least three office days per week
The immediate abolition of all office work
questions.explanation: 第 3 段提供了作答依据。正确选项用不同说法表达了文中的信息；请比较范围、数量、因果关系与限定词。
questions.evidence: Barclays Bank is one of latest big companies to do so, telling thousands of UK staff they must be in the office at least three days a week instead of two.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is explicitly made in paragraph 9?
options: Over the following two years of performance reviews, the performance of the hybrid workers was equal in quality to those who stayed in the office.
Those who came in around two days a week said they had a better work-life balance, more job satisfaction and less isolation than colleagues who came in more or less often.
And while it does not give a single magic number, the evidence does suggest that the best range is two or three days in the office – on the same days as your colleagues.
Use office days for the things that benefit from being in the same room, like brainstorming or mentoring new staff.
questions.explanation: 定位第 9 段，比较四个选项的具体信息。其余选项来自本文其他段落，并非本段明确陈述的内容。
questions.evidence: Those who came in around two days a week said they had a better work-life balance, more job satisfaction and less isolation than colleagues who came in more or less often.
